definitions.explanation: The jump-rope technique in which the rope is swung backward, from front to back, as the jumper hops over it — the reverse of the standard {前|まえ}{跳|と}び. Considered slightly harder because the rope cannot be seen as it approaches the feet.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{跳|と}びをやってみる。
examples.english: I'll try doing a backward jump.

examples.japanese: {後|うし}ろ{跳|と}びは⟦{前|まえ}{跳|と}び→前跳び：30927_maetobi⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{難|むずか}しい→難しい：00517_muzukashii⟧。
examples.english: The backward jump is harder than the forward jump.

examples.japanese: ⟦{縄|なわ}→縄：03511_nawa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{見|み}えない→見える：01165_mieru⟧ので、{後|うし}ろ{跳|と}びは⟦{最初|さいしょ}→最初：00882_saisho⟧、⟦{足|あし}→足：00575_ashi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{引|ひ}っかかった→引っかかる：12455_hikkakaru⟧。
examples.english: Since you can't see the rope, at first it kept catching on my feet when I did the backward jump.

notes:
{後|うし}ろ{跳|と}び reverses the direction of the rope: it is swung from front to back instead of back to front. Because the jumper cannot see the rope coming, it usually takes more practice than ⟦{前|まえ}{跳|と}び→前跳び：30927_maetobi⟧ to time the jump correctly.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{前|まえ}{跳|と}び→前跳び：30927_maetobi⟧: forward jump
- ⟦{交差|こうさ}{跳|と}び→交差跳び：30929_kousatobi⟧: cross jump
- ⟦{片足|かたあし}{跳|と}び→片足跳び：30930_kataashitobi⟧: single-leg jump

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {後|うし}ろ{跳|と}びをする: to do a backward jump
- {後|うし}ろ{跳|と}びができる: to be able to do a backward jump
